what: StandardAero repairs and overhauls aircraft engines. Airlines and operators send engines to its shops for the scheduled heavy maintenance that keeps them certified to fly.
customers: Commercial airlines, business jet operators, cargo carriers and military customers.
money: overhaul and repair of commercial and business jet engines
moat: Authorisations from engine makers to overhaul specific engine types, which are granted to few shops and take years and capital to obtain.
risks: $2.5B of debt against $290M of cash, from the private equity ownership before its 2024 listing
A 4.6% net margin: engine overhaul is labour-intensive
Engine makers increasingly want to do this work themselves
opportunities: Revenue grew from $4.2B to $6.1B in three years
Analysts see about 27% upside, with 14 covering the stock
Older aircraft are being kept flying longer because new deliveries are late, which means more overhauls
watch: Engine shop visit volumes and the margin per visit.
